title: Anglicans and Catholics
hook: decades of dialogue and shared prayer

segments.voice: Yesterday, spiritual ecumenism: prayer and a change of heart, the soul of Christian unity. Your line was prayer first.

A pope and an archbishop of Canterbury meet in Rome. Their churches have been apart a long time, with plenty of bitter history between them. They pray together and sign a declaration. Then, the story goes, Pope Paul the Sixth does something no document asked for. He takes the ring from his own finger and slips it onto the hand of Archbishop Michael Ramsey. Ramsey, by the usual telling, wore it for the rest of his life.
screen: `A POPE AND AN ARCHBISHOP IN ROME.` → `A RING FROM HIS OWN FINGER.` → `WORN FOR THE REST OF HIS LIFE.`

segments.voice: Who are Anglicans? The Church of England, and the churches around the world in communion with the archbishop of Canterbury, form the Anglican Communion. Its worship grew from the English Reformation, and Catholics and Anglicans have long disagreed about the papacy, the ordained ministry and more. Those disagreements are real, and neither side pretends otherwise. After that meeting in Rome, the two churches set up a joint commission of theologians, known by its initials as ARCIC. It has worked through hard questions, the Eucharist, ministry, authority, Mary, and published agreed statements, saying plainly where they agree and where they still don't. And look at what they already share. Anglican evening prayer, in the Book of Common Prayer, ends with collects, short prayers, and tradition traces one of them to an older Latin evening prayer. In the 1662 book it reads: "Lighten our darkness, we beseech thee, O Lord; and by thy great mercy defend us from all perils and dangers of this night; for the love of thy only Son, our Saviour, Jesus Christ. Amen." A Catholic praying night prayer and an Anglican saying evensong are, at that moment, asking for nearly the same thing. Last, the ring. A gift between friends doesn't settle a quarrel. It says the quarrel isn't the whole relationship. Later popes and archbishops of Canterbury have kept meeting, praying side by side and traveling together. That's yesterday's line, prayer first, at work: the friendship comes before the paperwork, and keeps the paperwork honest.
screen: `REAL DISAGREEMENTS, NAMED PLAINLY.` · `A COMMISSION FOR THE HARD QUESTIONS.` · `ONE EVENING PRAYER, TWO BOOKS.` · `A RING IS NOT A TREATY.` · then, large: `LIGHTEN OUR DARKNESS.`

segments.voice: Let an Anglican or Episcopal church you've passed come into view, or someone you know who worships there, and picture their evening service: candles, perhaps a choir, the old words read aloud. If you pray, pray for them, perhaps with the collect you just heard, lighten our darkness. If you don't, hold them in mind with goodwill, a neighbor down the road.
Anglicans and Catholics. Two churches long apart, still disagreeing honestly, and still praying side by side. Today's word.
Your line: old friends. Two churches, still apart, still praying side by side. That's day one thousand four hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: Catholics and Anglicans continue an official theological dialogue through a joint international commission, and their leaders meet and pray together. Locally, parishes sometimes share services of prayer for Christian unity.
